text:
maria: Started a quick canary run to compare microbatch sizing for streaming chat vs non-streaming completions. Baseline config attached.

maria: Baseline = 
```
model: redwood-3b-quant
mode: streaming (chat)
mb_size: 8
kernel_hint: fused_attn
kv_cache: enabled
```

dmitri: Nice. What are the perf targets? p95/p99 SLOs?

maria: p95 < 180ms for chat tokens (end-to-end), p99 < 420ms. For non-streaming completions we target p95 < 260ms since batching tolerates more latency.

kevin: Early profiler shows kernel switch happening at seq_len=512 which kills tail for streaming when mb_size >= 16. p99 spikes coincide with kernel selection fallback.

aj: Can you paste the hotstack? Might be kernel fallback to generic matmul on the last token.

maria: Hotstack snippet: 
```
0  fused_attn_forward
1  fallback_generic_attention (slow)
2  kv_cache_load
3  dispatch_kernel
```

maria: When mb_size=8 streaming stays on fused_attn. At mb_size=16 we see mixed kernels and kv_cache contention (more MV operations), p95 slightly better but p99 worse.

sophie: Observed KV cache lock contention on the canary gpus? Are we seeing mutex waits?

kevin: Yes, perf counters show increased atomic ops during kv reads with higher mbsizes for streaming; for completions (non-streaming) higher mb_size improved throughput and tail stayed stable — because we batch whole sequences and kernel stays the same.

maria: Summary of experiment results (numbers are p50/p95/p99 in ms, token-only generation):
- streaming mb=8: 28 / 150 / 360
- streaming mb=16: 30 / 140 / 610  <-- worse p99 tail
- completions mb=32: 22 / 210 / 320  <-- throughput win, tail ok

aj: Interesting that streaming p95 improved at mb=16 but p99 regressed a lot. That suggests a small subset of requests hitting fallback path and KV thrash.

perf-bot: Automated profiler summary uploaded: s3://perf-reports/2412345678/canary-profile.html :eyes:

dmitri: Action items:
1) Add a kernel selection hysteresis to avoid flipping kernels for small increases in batch size. (kevin)
2) Add KV cache hot-path prefetch / lockless read experiment to reduce atomic ops. (sophie)
3) Run canary with streaming mb=12 and a pinned kernel hint to confirm tradeoffs. (maria)

kevin: For (1) propose heuristic: allow fused_attn for up to 20% extra mem occupancy beyond threshold and prefer it if it reduces kernel transitions. Patch ready in branch `kernel-hyst-2412`.

sophie: For (2) I'll prototype a read-path that uses per-shardReadBuffer + rcu-style pointer swap to avoid atomics; will bench on canary tomorrow.

maria: I'll run the mb=12 pinned-kernel job and post results here. If mb=12 holds p95/p99 we might set streaming default mb to 10 with auto-fallback to 8 under tail pressure.

aj: Also let's add a perf test that synthesizes mixed short/long chat flows to exercise kernel thresholds and KV hotness. Current unit tests are too uniform.

maria: Agreed. Pushing logs and a short write-up in the drive folder: drive/redwood/perf/mbstream-kvtail/2412345678.md

dmitri: Thanks all. If mb=12 preserves tail we can update routing defaults for streaming vs completions separately. :+1:
